dose_adult.indication: Transtorno bipolar I, episódios maníacos ou mistos agudos (monoterapia)
dose_adult.note: Como adjuvante de lítio ou valproato, início de 10 a 15 mg/dia. Adjuvante no transtorno depressivo maior (seção 2.3): início de 2 a 5 mg/dia, faixa de 2 a 15 mg/dia. Ajustes por CYP2D6/CYP3A4 na seção 2.6.

cite.quote: The recommended starting dose in adults is 15 mg given once daily as monotherapy and 10 mg to 15 mg given once daily as adjunctive therapy with lithium or valproate.
cite.note: Mesma seção: "The recommended target dose of ABILIFY is 15 mg/day, as monotherapy or as adjunctive therapy with lithium or valproate. The dose may be increased to 30 mg/day based on clinical response. The safety of doses above 30 mg/day has not been evaluated in clinical trials."

cite.locator: Boxed warning: Increased mortality in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis
cite.quote: Elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis treated with antipsychotic drugs are at an increased risk of death.

cite.locator: Boxed warning: Suicidal thoughts and behaviors with antidepressant drugs
cite.quote: Antidepressants increased the risk of suicidal thoughts and behavior in children, adolescents, and young adults in short-term studies.
If signs and symptoms of tardive dyskinesia appear in a patient on ABILIFY, drug discontinuation should be considered.

Atypical antipsychotic drugs have been associated with metabolic changes that include hyperglycemia/diabetes mellitus, dyslipidemia, and body weight gain. While all drugs in the class have been shown to produce some metabolic changes, each drug has its own specific risk profile.
cite.note: Mesma seção: "There have been reports of hyperglycemia in patients treated with ABILIFY". Nos ensaios em adultos, glicemia e lipídios não diferiram significativamente do placebo.

cite.quote: ABILIFY may cause orthostatic hypotension, perhaps due to its alpha 1 -adrenergic receptor antagonism.

In clinical trials and/or postmarketing experience, events of leukopenia and neutropenia have been reported temporally related to antipsychotic agents, including ABILIFY. Agranulocytosis has also been reported.
As with other antipsychotic drugs, ABILIFY should be used cautiously in patients with a history of seizures or with conditions that lower the seizure threshold.

cite.locator: seção 7.1 Drugs Having Clinically Important Interactions with ABILIFY
cite.quote: The intensity of sedation was greater with the combination of oral aripiprazole and lorazepam as compared to that observed with aripiprazole alone.
cite.note: Mesma tabela: "Monitor sedation and blood pressure. Adjust dose accordingly."

cite.locator: seção 7.1 Drugs Having Clinically Important Interactions with ABILIFY
cite.quote: Reduce the ABILIFY dosage when administered concomitantly with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor or a strong CYP2D6 inhibitor
cite.note: Seção 2.6 (Tabela 1): metade da dose usual com inibidor potente de CYP2D6 (ex.: fluoxetina, paroxetina) e também em metabolizadores lentos de CYP2D6. No uso adjuvante no transtorno depressivo maior, a bula manda não ajustar.

cite.locator: seção 2.6 Dosage Adjustments for Cytochrome P450 Considerations
cite.quote: Dosage adjustments are recommended in patients who are known CYP2D6 poor metabolizers and in patients taking concomitant CYP3A4 inhibitors or CYP2D6 inhibitors or strong CYP3A4 inducers
cite.note: Tabela 1: metade da dose com inibidor potente de CYP3A4 (ex.: itraconazol, claritromicina); dobrar a dose em 1 a 2 semanas com indutor potente (ex.: carbamazepina, rifampicina). No uso adjuvante no transtorno depressivo maior, a bula manda não ajustar.

cite.quote: Neonates exposed to antipsychotic drugs, including ABILIFY, during the third trimester of pregnancy are at risk for extrapyramidal and/or withdrawal symptoms following delivery
aripiprazole exposure during pregnancy and/or the postpartum period may lead to clinically relevant decreases in milk supply which may be reversible with discontinuation of the drug
cite.note: Mesma seção: "Monitor the breastfed infant for dehydration and lack of appropriate weight gain."

cite.locator: Boxed warning: Suicidal thoughts and behaviors with antidepressant drugs
cite.quote: In patients of all ages who are started on antidepressant therapy, monitor closely for worsening, and for emergence of suicidal thoughts and behaviors.
Weight gain has been observed with atypical antipsychotic use. Clinical monitoring of weight is recommended.
cite.note: Mesma seção: glicemia de jejum no início e periodicamente para quem tem fatores de risco para diabetes, e acompanhamento do controle glicêmico em quem já tem diabetes.
